output.summary: The deterministic capacity verdict is NO_POLICY: no capacity policy was defined, and the analysis provided only a LOWER_BOUND capacity summary with lower_inclusive=20 users, capacity_knee=null (knee_reason KNEE_DETECTOR_NOT_IMPLEMENTED) and upper_exclusive=null (analysis-result.json#/capacity_summary, analysis-result.json#/policy_verdict). All three ramp stages (r1-users5, r1-users10, r1-users20) completed 30/30 bins, achieved their target load within tolerance, and passed the defined error-rate check (0 errors on 132,623 overall samples) and the generator CPU-throttle diagnostic (threshold 0.2 ratio, PASS for every stage with observed max 0.059/0.149/0.13). The windows' business_verdict is PASS while resource_verdict is NO_POLICY, and findings are empty. Interpretation limits: the run validates only the tested load range up to 20 users; it does not establish an upper capacity bound, a knee, spare capacity, or the absence of problems beyond 20 users. Clock alignment is not_verified_by_core, so no temporal/lead-lag causal claims are supported until clock verification is done.

hypotheses.observation: All three stages (r1-users5, r1-users10, r1-users20) completed 30/30 expected bins, achieved the target load within 10% tolerance, and produced PASS window verdicts; the capacity summary reports bound_type LOWER_BOUND with lower_inclusive=20, capacity_knee=null, knee_reason=KNEE_DETECTOR_NOT_IMPLEMENTED, and upper_exclusive=null.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: The application sustained up to 20 concurrent users without tripping the defined error-rate check, but this only verifies a lower bound on capacity; the actual knee or upper limit remains unknown because the knee detector was not implemented and no higher load stage was run.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Run additional ramp stages above 20 users (e.g., 40, 80, 160) with a usable knee-detection rule until an upper exclusive bound or knee is observed, and confirm each stage completes 30 bins at the target load.

hypotheses.observation: Recorded CPU for monitored services is low at the tested loads: checkoutservice mean CPU ranges ~0.047-0.068 cores, frontend ~0.184-0.187 cores, paymentservice ~0.012-0.015 cores across the three windows.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: At 5-20 users the services appear lightly utilized, which could indicate headroom — but this is a hypothesis, not proof of spare capacity, since utilization response beyond 20 users was never measured.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Extend the load profile upward while watching checkoutservice, frontend, and paymentservice cpu_cores series to measure how utilization responds to load and where degradation begins.

hypotheses.observation: Generator cfs_throttled_period_ratio maxima increased across windows (0.059 in r1-users5, 0.149 in r1-users10, 0.13 in r1-users20) while every resource-policy-check for the generator rule (operator gt, threshold 0.2) reported PASS; medians and q05 are 0 throughout.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: Occasional throttling/scheduling episodes occur on the jmeter-generator host rather than sustained throttling, and they currently stay below the 0.2 threshold; if peak throttling grows with further load it could distort generator timing and load accuracy.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Correlate the throttling peaks with generator host CPU quotas and scheduler behavior, and verify clock alignment between generator and monitored services before attributing any cause to those episodes.

hypotheses.observation: Overall load test recorded 132,623 samples with 0 errors; overall latency_ms max 2406, p99 298; per-transaction p99 values include product 665 ms and home 462 ms, and the cart transaction has max 2406 ms.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: A long-tail latency distribution exists even at 20 users (possible GC pauses, cold caches, or mixed-service variance), and whether the tail grows with load has not been tested because no per-window latency policy was defined.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Compute per-window latency percentiles per transaction from the JTL and test whether p99/max grows with user count, correlating any spikes with resource series in the same windows.

hypotheses.observation: In the r1-users5 window, paymentservice memory_bytes has a positive slope_per_second of 12458 bytes/s and split_half_shift of 1093632 bytes; in the r1-users10 window the slope is -975 bytes/s.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: Possible early-window memory accumulation (allocation or caching) that may or may not plateau; the data are too short to establish a leak or a stable plateau.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Run a fixed-load soak at 20 users for a longer duration and inspect paymentservice memory_bytes slope and split-half trend to distinguish accumulation from plateau.

hypotheses.observation: Window policy summaries report business_verdict PASS and resource_verdict NO_POLICY for all three stages, the overall policy_verdict is NO_POLICY, and the findings list is empty.
hypotheses.possible_explanation: No capacity or service-level resource policy existed for this run (only the error-rate check and the generator-throttle diagnostic were defined), so the absence of flagged violations does not indicate policy compliance or stability.
hypotheses.recommended_check: Define explicit capacity and per-service resource policies (cpu_cores, memory_bytes, latency percentiles) before future runs so that PASS/FAIL verdicts become meaningful and enforceable.

recommendations.action: Verify and synchronize clocks across the JMeter generator and all monitored services (checkoutservice, frontend, paymentservice) before any temporal or lead/lag analysis.
recommendations.rationale: resource-binding records clock_alignment as not_verified_by_core; until clocks are verified, any ordering or causal interpretation built on these timestamps is unsupported.

recommendations.action: Extend the ramp beyond 20 users with a working knee detector to establish an upper exclusive capacity bound.
recommendations.rationale: The capacity summary is a LOWER_BOUND with lower_inclusive=20, upper_exclusive=null, and knee_reason=KNEE_DETECTOR_NOT_IMPLEMENTED, so the actual capacity limit has not been determined.

recommendations.action: Define explicit capacity and service-level resource policies (CPU, memory, latency) for future runs.
recommendations.rationale: Overall policy_verdict is NO_POLICY and each window shows resource_verdict NO_POLICY, so current PASS results only cover the defined error-rate check and generator-throttle diagnostic; a missing policy is not a pass.

recommendations.action: Track generator cfs_throttled_period_ratio maxima as load increases and add a margin below the 0.2 threshold for generator health.
recommendations.rationale: The generator-throttle checks all PASS, but observed maxima rose to 0.149 (r1-users10) and 0.13 (r1-users20), which could distort load generation if it grows further.

recommendations.action: Investigate the latency tail per window and per transaction, especially cart max 2406 ms, product p99 665 ms, and home p99 462 ms.
recommendations.rationale: Overall latency has a long tail (overall p99 298 ms, max 2406 ms) even though errors are 0; without per-window latency analysis it is unknown whether tail latency grows with load.

recommendations.action: Run a longer fixed-load soak at 20 users and monitor paymentservice memory_bytes slope and split-half shift over time.
recommendations.rationale: Paymentservice memory shows a positive slope (12458 bytes/s) and split-half shift of 1093632 bytes in the 5-user window, so a longer observation is needed to determine whether memory plateaus or accumulates.

caveats: Capacity knee detection was not implemented (knee_reason=KNEE_DETECTOR_NOT_IMPLEMENTED) and upper_exclusive is null, so only the tested lower bound of 20 users is verified; no upper-bound or knee capacity claim is supported.

Overall policy_verdict is NO_POLICY and each window's resource_verdict is NO_POLICY; PASS verdicts apply only to the defined error-rate check and generator-throttle diagnostic, and a missing policy must not be read as a pass.
Clock alignment is not_verified_by_core (resource-binding), so no lead/lag ordering or temporal causal hypothesis can be supported until clocks are verified.
Load was only exercised up to 20 users; low observed CPU values do not prove spare capacity or the absence of saturation, errors, or latency problems at higher load.

Zero errors across the sampled JMeter transactions (132,623 overall samples) does not prove the absence of all functional issues; coverage is limited to the sampled transactions (add product to cart, cart, checkout, home, product, reset cart).
The empty findings list does not by itself prove stability or the absence of anomalies; it only reflects what the defined checks detected.
Evidence covers the evaluation interval from epoch ms 1790634210000 to 1790635250000 (about 1040 s) inside a wider run/snapshot span; long-run or soak behavior at steady load was not evaluated.
Only a generator CPU-throttle resource diagnostic is present; there are no service-level cpu_cores or memory_bytes policy checks (NO_POLICY), so service-level resource limits remain undefined.
